CVE-2026-102918.title: Redux Framework <= 4.5.15 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via multi_media Field and Client-Supplied checkuser_id

This is due to the field's renderer printing the stored value into an href attribute, a hidden input value and an HTML element without escaping, while every neighbouring attribute in the same method is wrapped in esc_attr(). CVE-2026-110737.description:
The push endpoint of a Vaadin application that uses server push reflects the request Origin into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header and allows credentials, because Flow configures Atmosphere with DROP_ACCESS_CONTROL_ALLOW_ORIGIN_HEADER set to false and its CorsInterceptor then echoes whatever Origin the request carries. CVE-2026-111103.title: HTTP/2 StreamError recovery rolls back connection state and bypasses per-connection limits in Bandit
CVE-2026-111103.description:
Improper Cleanup on Thrown Exception vulnerability in the HTTP/2 handler of mtrudel bandit allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass per-connection resource limits via a single TCP write that carries several frames, one of which raises a stream error.

When a frame raises StreamError partway through a chunk, Bandit.HTTP2.Handler.handle_data/3 sends RST_STREAM and continues with the connection state from before the chunk, dropping the rest of it. Streams opened by earlier frames in the chunk keep running their Plug calls, but the stream counts, last_stream_id, the rapid-reset timestamps, the HPACK decoder state and the buffer roll back, so max_concurrent_streams, max_requests and the rapid-reset limiter never see those streams. A client that sends one HEADERS frame more than max_concurrent_streams in each write has the extra refused and the others forgotten: with a limit of 10, five such writes run 50 Plug calls at once.

This issue affects bandit: from 1.9.0 before 1.14.0.

CVE-2026-129438.title: Incorrect RFC 3986 URI serialization for oversized input
CVE-2026-129438.description:
Incorrect RFC 3986 URI serialization for oversized input.

The Uri\Rfc3986\Uri class does not correctly handle the output-size limit and errors of the uriparser library when converting a URI back to a string. For a URI whose string representation reaches approximately 2 GiB, toString(), toRawString() and other serializing operations can return a truncated or invalid string instead of an error. An application that accepts attacker-controlled URI data of that size, has enough memory to process it and trusts the result may make incorrect validation or routing decisions, and the large allocations can exhaust memory. parse_url() and Uri\WhatWg\Url are not affected.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

CVE-2026-98938.title: rust: irq: pass RegistrationInner as cookie to request_irq
CVE-2026-98938.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

rust: irq: pass RegistrationInner as cookie to request_irq

With commit ba268514ea14 ("rust: devres: fix race condition due to
nesting"), Devres::new() returns Result<Self> by value instead of
initializing in-place via PinInit. Because request_irq() is called
inside Devres::new(), registration.inner is still uninitialized when the
IRQ is enabled, so accessing registration.inner.device() in the IRQ
callback can read uninitialized memory.

Fix this by storing the Device and handler pointer in RegistrationInner
and passing RegistrationInner as the IRQ cookie after its fields are
initialized.

This is not needed in mainline because commit 98c63ce4d760 ("rust: irq:
make Registration compatible with lifetime-bound drivers") removed
Devres from irq::Registration and moved request_irq() after all fields
are initialized.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: sparx5: free the matchall entry on destroy

sparx5_tc_matchall_replace() allocates a struct sparx5_mall_entry for
every offloaded matchall filter and adds it to sparx5->mall_entries.
sparx5_tc_matchall_destroy() removes the entry from the list, but never

deleting matchall mirror and goto filters. With the fix, kmemleak no
longer reports the leak.

CVE-2026-99461.title: mm: khugepaged: fix swap entry value to folio_pfn()
CVE-2026-99461.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm: khugepaged: fix swap entry value to folio_pfn()

Patch series "mm: khugepaged: fix tracepoint UAF", v5.

The khugepaged tracepoints take a folio pointer and call folio_pfn(), but
by then the folio may no longer be valid: freed after folio_put(),
folio_unlock() or pte_unmap_unlock(), or not a folio at all but an
xarray-encoded swap entry. On classic SPARSEMEM, dereferencing it oopses
khugepaged as soon as the trace event is enabled; on other memory models
it merely prints a bogus pfn.

Pass the pfn to the tracepoints directly, captured while the folio is
still pinned, closing the use-after-free windows in
mm_khugepaged_scan_file(), mm_khugepaged_scan_pmd() and
mm_khugepaged_collapse_file().

CVE-2026-99586.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

iommu/arm-smmu-v3: Handle ARM erratum for CONT under invalidation with SVA

The erratum (MMU-700: #3777127, S3: #3673557) deals with under
invalidation of a CONT PTE grouping in the SMMU. The recommended work
around is to use a range invalidation that spans the entire CONT. The only
user of CONT in the kernel right now is through SVA sharing a CPU page
table that contains a CONT created by the mm.

Previously it was thought that this errata was dealt with because the
driver always uses range invalidation. However, there is a subtle detail
in the errata that the invalidation range must fully enclose the entire
CONT for it to work.

CVE-2026-99605.title: drm/etnaviv: Fix NULL dereference on unbind without PPU flop reset
CVE-2026-99605.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/etnaviv: Fix NULL dereference on unbind without PPU flop reset

flop_reset_data_ppu is only allocated on GPUs that need the PPU flop
reset. However, etnaviv_unbind(..) frees it unconditionally, and
etnaviv_cmdbuf_free(..) dereferences cmdbuf->suballoc before checking
whether cmdbuf is NULL.

As a result, unloading the driver on GPUs that do not need the PPU
flop reset causes a NULL pointer dereference at address 0.
